rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the most informative first step is to establish a simple, reliable baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest configuration in the search space: it uses a standard, low-risk encoder (PCA), the simplest profile setting, and no aggregation or fusion complexity. This gives us a clear accuracy floor for the RNA modality. In subsequent experiments, we can test image-only (config_010/013) to compare modalities, then explore better RNA encoders (scvi, scgpt) or multimodal fusion, always benchmarking against this baseline. Starting simple minimizes the risk of confounding multiple design choices and provides the reference point needed to interpret all later results within the 10-experiment budget.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only/singleprofile/pca_n2000 at ~48.5% accuracy), the most critical uncertainty is whether the image modality carries meaningful signal for this task. Config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) provides a clean, single-variable comparison to config_001 by swapping only the modality while holding profile setting (singleprofile) constant. If image alone performs comparably or better than RNA alone, multimodal fusion becomes a high-priority direction for the remaining 8 experiments. If image performs poorly, I can redirect budget toward improving the RNA representation (scvi, scgpt) or multiprofile aggregation. This experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the modality axis before committing budget to more complex multimodal configurations.

Evidence: RNA (PCA n2000, single profile) achieves 0.485 accuracy while Image (ResNet50, single profile) only reaches 0.208, establishing RNA as the dominant modality by a wide margin. Uncertainty: We do not yet know whether multiprofile aggregation provides meaningful additional signal over a single profile, or whether the encoder is the bottleneck. This experiment tests whether moving from single to multiprofile with the same PCA encoder and the simplest aggregation (avgpool) improves on the RNA baseline. It is the most direct, minimal extension of the best result (config_001), isolating the effect of profile multiplicity. If multiprofile helps, it opens a path to test transformer aggregation (config_003); if it does not, it redirects attention toward encoder quality (scvi/scgpt). With 7 experiments remaining, this is the highest-information next step for improving the dominant modality.

Evidence: config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) achieved 0.591 acc, a large improvement over config_001 (singleprofile, 0.485), confirming multiprofile aggregation is highly beneficial. Image alone (config_010) is very weak (0.208), so multimodal gains are uncertain. Question: Does transformer aggregation outperform avgpool for multiprofile RNA? This experiment (config_003) isolates exactly one variable—aggregation method—while holding model setting, profile setting, and encoder fixed to the best-performing combination. Why now: With 6 experiments remaining, establishing whether transformer or avgpool is superior for aggregation will directly inform the aggregation choice for all subsequent multimodal experiments (configs 018-051), making this the highest-leverage controlled comparison at this stage.

The best result so far is config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) at 0.591 acc, showing that multiprofile + avgpool is the strongest RNA configuration. The key remaining uncertainty for the RNA pathway is whether a learned nonlinear encoder (scvi_n200) can outperform the linear PCA baseline. Config_005 isolates exactly this variable—changing only the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 while holding profile (multiprofile) and aggregation (avgpool) fixed—giving a clean comparison against config_002. This is the highest-value next step because: (1) RNA dominates over image (0.485 vs 0.208), so improving the RNA representation is the most impactful lever; (2) if scvi improves on PCA, it establishes a stronger backbone before exploring multimodal fusion; (3) if it does not, PCA is confirmed as sufficient and we can redirect remaining budget toward fusion or image-encoder questions. With 5 experiments left after this one, resolving the encoder question now prevents wasted budget on multimodal configs built on a suboptimal RNA representation.

Evidence: The current best (config_005: rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) achieves 0.650 accuracy. We've confirmed multiprofile+avgpool is the best profile/aggregation combo (0.591 vs 0.485 and 0.519 for singleprofile/transformer with pca). The key remaining uncertainty in the RNA-only pipeline is whether the scgpt encoder outperforms scvi_n200 under identical conditions. Question: config_008 (rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, avgpool) isolates the encoder effect by changing only the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 to scgpt while holding multiprofile+avgpool fixed. Why this is the best use: With 4 experiments remaining, identifying the best encoder is critical before committing to multimodal fusion experiments. If scgpt matches or beats scvi_n200, it opens a new high-performing branch; if not, we confirm scvi_n200 as optimal and can direct remaining budget toward multimodal combinations with the best encoder. This is a clean single-variable comparison that maximally reduces uncertainty about the most impactful design choice.

The current best is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 acc. For pca_n2000, avgpool clearly outperformed transformer (0.591 vs 0.519), but the optimal aggregation may differ for scvi_n200's learned latent representations. config_006 is a clean single-variable comparison (only aggregation changes from avgpool to transformer) that directly tests whether transformer aggregation could unlock further gains with the best-performing encoder. This is the highest-value exploitation step: it either confirms avgpool as the correct aggregation (freeing the remaining 3 experiments to explore multimodal fusion with scvi_n200) or discovers a new best configuration to build upon. Given the weak image-only signal (0.208), solidifying the RNA-only ceiling before adding a second modality is the prudent use of this experiment.

Evidence: The best configuration so far is config_006 (RNA-only, scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer) at 0.653 acc. RNA clearly dominates (0.485–0.653) over image-only resnet50 (0.208). The scvi_n200 encoder with multiprofile is the strongest RNA pipeline, and transformer≈avgpool for it. The only untested image encoder is imagenet_vit_l, which is substantially larger and likely more informative than resnet50. Question: Can adding a strong image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) to the best RNA pipeline (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer) via concat fusion beat the RNA-only ceiling of 0.653? Why this is the best use of experiment 8: With only 2 experiments remaining, we need to directly test whether multimodal fusion can improve on the current best. Resnet50-based multimodal is unlikely to help given its 0.208 image-only score, so imagenet_vit_l is the only viable image path. This configuration isolates the multimodal question using the already-validated best RNA settings, and if it succeeds we secure a new best; if it fails, the remaining experiment can test weighted fusion or confirm RNA-only as optimal.

The current best is config_038 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) at 0.721 accuracy. The evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 as the best RNA encoder (~0.65 RNA-only), multiprofile over single profile, transformer aggregation over avgpool (0.653 vs 0.650), and imagenet_vit_l over resnet50 (image-only resnet50 was 0.208). The one remaining untested dimension for this top configuration is the fusion strategy: concat (tested, 0.721) vs weighted. Config_039 isolates exactly this single variable (weighted fusion) while holding all other settings identical to the best. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, testing the most direct extension of the current best is the highest-value use of the slot: it either finds a new best or confirms concat is optimal, reducing uncertainty about the final answer.

The current best is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, ViT-L, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250. The only untested variants that keep all winning components (scvi_n200, ViT-L, multiprofile, weighted fusion) are config_036 and config_037, which swap transformer for avgpool aggregation. Config_037 (avgpool + weighted) is the most controlled single-variable test: it isolates whether transformer aggregation truly matters in the multimodal fusion context, since in the RNA-only setting the transformer/avgpool gap was minimal (0.653 vs 0.650). As the final experiment, this is a pure exploitation play on the most promising region of the search space. If it matches or exceeds 0.7250, we gain a new best; if not, we confirm transformer aggregation is the correct choice, giving a clean final answer. No other untested config has a realistic chance of beating the current best given the strong evidence favoring scvi_n200, ViT-L, multiprofile, and weighted fusion.
